content: In a browser check against a TanStack Query app, a read made right after a mutation or a route change sees the cached data while the refetch is still in flight. Wait on the expected value (`waitForFunction(() => el.textContent.includes("300"))`) or a heading unique to the new route, never on the element merely existing. Only then decide it's a bug.
context: Fuel page session, 2026-09-26: four separate "failures" were this exact race and not defects. /fuel still showed Start's h1 (T-051), the foods list read 0 "Save it" rows (T-050), the first chip was still the old one after saving a food (T-050), and the Day view showed "no target" just after carbs were set to 300 g (T-054). One real defect looked the same and wasn't the race: the fuel row showing old numbers right after "Save" (T-046). That one was fixed by awaiting the refetch in onSuccess. The way to tell them apart is to wait for the value; if it never arrives, it's real.
title: After a write, wait for the value you expect — don't read the page right after navigating
